newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo cen.bank official sees zero inflation in "97.
newsitem.headline: Yugo cen.bank official sees zero inflation in "97.

text.p: Yugoslavia will have zero growth in retail prices in 1997, a senior central bank official said on Monday.
"In December 1997 there will be zero growth in retail prices compared to December 1996," the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) Vice-Governor Ratko Banovic said.
Yugoslavia is entering 1997 without price pressures, he said and recalled that the country had entered 1995 and 1996 with pronounced price tensions.

"In September we had 1.1 percent monthly inflation, in October it stood at 1.3 and in November at 1.8 percent. But during the first ten days of December prices fell by 1 percent," Banovic told a meeting of businessmen and bankers.
The last quarter of 1996 was marked by subdued monetary developments, he said.

"Usually, the fourth quarter is very tense in terms of monetary developments, but we have acted on time and launched a series of measures in August to prevent the monetary sphere from overstraining and to calm down monetary aggregates," he said.
The central bank in August launched a 10 percent reserve requirement to halt expanding credit activity in the banking sector and prevent the discount rate from rising.

According to some estimates, the average 1997 inflation rate carried over from 1996 will stand at around 17.4 percent. In 1996, the carried-over inflation stood close to 44 percent. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
